question_text: 1. (a) Which kind of garbage is not converted into compost by the redworms? (b) Have you seen any other organism besides redworms, in your pit? If yes, try to find out their names. Draw pictures of these.

mcq_options.option_text: Which kind of garbage is not converted into compost by the redworms?
Have you seen any other organism besides redworms, in your pit? If yes, try to find out their names. Draw pictures of these.

parts.part_text: Which kind of garbage is not converted into compost by the redworms?
parts.answer_text: The garbage which are non-biodegradable in nature like iron strips, plastics, poly bags etc. are not converted into compost by the redworms.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, non-biodegradable garbage is not converted into compost by redworms.

parts.part_text: Have you seen any other organism besides redworms, in your pit? If yes, try to find out their names. Draw pictures of these.
parts.answer_text: Yes, these organisms include maggots, flies, cockroaches etc.
parts.final_answer: These organisms can be found in the compost pit.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of composting and identification of organisms.

question_text: 2. Discuss : (a) Is garbage disposal the responsibility only of the government? (b) Is it possible to reduce the problems relating to disposal of garbage?

mcq_options.option_text: Is garbage disposal the responsibility only of the government?
Is it possible to reduce the problems relating to disposal of garbage?

parts.part_text: Is garbage disposal the responsibility only of the government?
parts.answer_text: No, garbage disposal is not only the responsibility of the government. It is the sole responsibility of both government and the people.
parts.final_answer: Each citizen must be responsible for maintaining proper sanitation.

parts.part_text: Is it possible to reduce the problems relating to disposal of garbage?
parts.answer_text: Yes, it is possible to reduce the problems relating to disposal of garbage by taking measures such as generating less waste and recycling.
parts.final_answer: Awareness and efficient use of products can help reduce garbage disposal issues.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding societal responsibilities and waste management strategies.

question_text: 5. (a) Collect different kinds of packaging material. What was the purpose for which each one was used? Discuss in groups. (b) Give an example in which packaging could have been reduced? (c) Write a story on how packaging increases the amount of garbage.

mcq_options.option_text: Collect different kinds of packaging material. What was the purpose for which each one was used? Discuss in groups.
Give an example in which packaging could have been reduced?
Write a story on how packaging increases the amount of garbage.

parts.part_text: Collect different kinds of packaging material. What was the purpose for which each one was used?
parts.answer_text: Different kinds of packaging materials and their uses include: (i) Paper packaging materials: Used for packing light and durable products like soaps, chocolates. (ii) Plastic packaging materials: Used for liquid items like oils, drinking water bottles. (iii) Poly bags: Used for carrying groceries. (iv) Clothes and Jute packaging materials: Used for carrying clothes, grains.
parts.final_answer: Various materials serve specific purposes in packaging.

parts.part_text: Give an example in which packaging could have been reduced?
parts.answer_text: If people started carrying their own carry bags for buying groceries and vegetables, then there will be no need for packing those materials by using plastics.
parts.final_answer: Using personal bags can significantly reduce packaging waste.

parts.part_text: Write a story on how packaging increases the amount of garbage.
parts.answer_text: Packaging increases the amount of garbage as it is often discarded after the product is used. Many packaging materials can't be reused and contribute to waste, especially plastics.
parts.final_answer: Excessive packaging leads to significant environmental waste.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves analysis of packaging materials and their environmental impact.

question_text: 6. Do you think it is better to use compost instead of chemical fertilisers? Why?
answer_text: Yes, I think it is better to use compost instead of chemical fertilisers because: (i) It is environment friendly and adds natural fertility to the soil. (ii) It doesn't have adverse effects on nature and creates no pollution. (iii) The food items grown are also healthy and do not contain any chemicals. (iv) It is cheaper than chemical fertiliser. (v) Soil will never lose its fertility if we use compost.
final_answer: Using compost is beneficial for the environment and soil health.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of environmental benefits of composting.
